newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cement firm ups profits in H1.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cement firm ups profits in H1.

text.p: Egyptian Tora Portland Cement increased its net after-tax profits to 78.5 million pounds ($23 million) in the first half of the 1996/7 financial year from 63.45 million in the same period of the previous year.
The financial year ends on June 30.
In a published announcement, the firm said its sales also went up to 280.6 million between July and December 1996 from 235.8 million in the first half of 1995/6.

The state retains 67.5 percent of the firm, which has a total of 23.841 million shares, while private shareholders own about 22.5 percent. The employee shareholder association holds the remaining 10 percent.
Tora shares ended at the Cairo stock market on Sunday at 97.00 pounds, slightly down from 97.49 on Thursday.
The firm distributed 5.75 pounds per share for the 1995/6 financial year, against 4.75 pounds for the previous year.
